_comment: ccfleet config. Every value here is fictional. Keep your real one outside any public repo: it names your repos and carries your principal's words.
_claude_args: None here on purpose. A headless session has no one to ask: whatever these grant, it does unattended with your credentials. Add the narrowest permission mode and tool rules that do the work; `ccfleet check` names any you set, and `man ccfleet` (THREATS) says what can steer such a session.
_settings: With claude_args, the whole grant: no user-level settings load, and a session gets your user-level settings less their allow rules, default mode, extra directories and approving hooks, with these on top. `ccfleet check` prints what is left out and each hook kept.
_drop_hooks: Texts naming user-level hooks to leave out of every session, such as one whose script approves tool calls.
_instructions_guard: refuse (the default): a public or unknown-visibility repo's launch is refused when the user-level CLAUDE.md every session gets names a private name; warn: append it anyway, with a line per name.
_vars: Template values for every job. The principal's word to finish cut-off passes (FINISH_WORDS) is never kept here: each resume and fold passes it per call (--set FINISH_WORDS=...), from his words for that reset, and ccfleet does not check it.

vars.ASK: "Bring every repo up to a healthy state." (the principal's words, quoted verbatim from your own record)
vars.REVIEW_APPROVAL: No review-tier work is approved for this run.
vars.APPROVAL: "Run the briefed reviews until the budget is used." (the principal's words, verbatim, for this drain only)
vars.PROVENANCE: This drain session wrote no brief and started no writer of any pass it runs.

example-app.notes: CI was red on the lint job at the last sweep.

example-docs.notes: Public: everything written here is published.

example-infra.notes: No remote: local master is the mainline (branch is read only for a repo with no remote). Reads of live systems only; no writes.

_queue: Your own queue tool; ccfleet only calls it. It must keep the seal contract (man ccfleet, THE QUEUE INTERFACE): ranked, next and take refuse until this run's ranking is sealed, by a seal command ccfleet never calls. instruments/fixtures/review_queue_reference.py keeps it, with this exact command shape.
